tier_reason: First-party: the README chart (thorvg.site readme/example_performance.png) gives ThorVG vs Skia v148 CPU fps per test and the harness is public (thorvg/thorvg.benchmark src/thorvg/*_thorvg_sdl.cpp, src/skia/*_skia_sdl.cpp, src/common/benchmark_runner.hpp) with Apple M2 Pro stated, but no compiler is named and flags are only implied by build instructions (CMake Release harness, ThorVG meson defaults, Skia from vcpkg), so not A; no independent measurement, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'an average of ~2.9x faster' than 'a widely-used vector graphics engine' (Skia v148 in the test conditions), CPU backend, 2560x1440, 5k primitives. Chart table (fps, ThorVG vs Skia): Rects 76.0 vs 17.2 (4.4x), Rotated Rects 36.0 vs 10.1 (3.6x), Stroke 55.7 vs 17.2 (3.2x), Rects+Stroke 41.8 vs 10.5 (4.0x), Rotated Rects+Stroke 25.0 vs 4.5 (5.6x), Circles 38.5 vs 10.4 (3.7x), Images (PNG) 6.4 vs 6.0 (1.1x), Rotated Images 4.4 vs 4.4 (1.0x), Linear Gradient 9.0 vs 8.5 (1.1x), Radial Gradient 6.9 vs 6.0 (1.2x). The 2.9x is the arithmetic mean of the ten per-test ratios (2.89, derived from page data); image and gradient cases are roughly at parity.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Compiler not stated (macOS build, presumably Apple Clang). thorvg.benchmark README: harness built with CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release; ThorVG built with meson using project defaults (buildtype=debugoptimized, optimization=3); Skia installed from vcpkg (arm64-osx triplet), its build flags not stated.
corrections.hardware: Apple M2 Pro (macOS 26) per README test conditions
corrections.workload: thorvg.benchmark CPU backend at 2560x1440: 5,000 retained shapes per frame (rects with alpha 240-255, rotated rects, strokes, circles, PNG images with bilinear filtering, linear/radial gradients), per-frame translate/scale (and rotation in rotation mode), 120 warmup + 1000 measured frames, frame time includes SDL_UpdateWindowSurface for both engines.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark (thorvg/thorvg.benchmark, MIT, 6 stars). Thread asymmetry: the harness initialises ThorVG with opts.threads worker threads, default 4 since commit 2f87860 'thorvg: fine-tuned options' (2026-08-31; before that the default was hardware_concurrency), while Skia renders through a single-threaded raster surface (SkSurfaces::WrapPixels). The README chart was last updated the same day (2026-08-31) and the README does not state the thread count, so the ~2.9x compares multi-threaded ThorVG with single-threaded Skia; the gains are largest in geometry-heavy tests and near 1x for images and gradients. Compiler not named; Skia's vcpkg build flags unverified. The headline sentence does not name Skia (only the test conditions do). The stroke workload was replaced on 2026-09-21 (designer stroked paths) and the harness says new stroke results are not comparable with earlier runs, so the chart's Stroke row predates the current code. Per-test numbers exist only as an image.

notes: Numbers match the README chart exactly; 2.9x is the mean of per-test ratios. Main issue is fairness: ThorVG runs with 4 worker threads against single-threaded Skia raster in the benchmark harness, and the README omits this; consider a shortcoming. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 1.9k stars, not archived, last commit 2026-10-03.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the blocked results pages are readable from the gh-pages branch (x86_64.html, arm.html hold per-test ns for tiny-skia, Skia, cairo, raqote), the benchmark code is public (benches/src, benches/Cargo.toml with cairo-rs/skia-rs/raqote features, gen-charts-*.py), and benches/README.md states compilers and flags (rustc with -Ctarget-cpu=x86-64/haswell; Skia via clang with -march=x86-64/haswell and listed gn args; cairo 1.16.0 system gcc build with -march=native) and CPUs (AMD 3700X on Gentoo; Apple M1).

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 20-100% slower than Skia on x86-64 and about 100-300% slower on ARM, 'still faster than cairo and raqote in many cases'. Results pages (gh-pages x86_64.html, July 2021; arm.html, Aug 2022): tiny-skia AVX2 beats cairo in 41 of 49 x86 tests (geometric mean 2.27x, range 0.31x-11.9x) and tiny-skia beats cairo in 46 of 49 ARM tests (geometric mean 2.7x) (derived from page data). Cairo wins on x86 Rect fills (tiny-skia 0.37-0.45x), Nearest pattern (0.39x) and Source Over/Destination Over/Plus blending (0.31-0.58x); tiny-skia wins most on non-separable blend modes (4.5-9x), bicubic patterns (11.9x) and AA hairlines (4.4x). Against Skia AVX2 tiny-skia wins only 5 of 50 x86 tests (geometric mean 0.68x, derived).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: x86 page (committed 2021-07-04): benches/README at that time lists Rust 1.53 (nightly cargo bench), clang 12, tiny-skia -Ctarget-cpu=x86-64 (SSE2) or haswell (AVX2), Skia built with clang -march=x86-64/haswell plus -DSK_FORCE_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLITTER and is_debug=false gn args, cairo 1.16.0 Gentoo system build with gcc -march=native (gcc version and -O level not stated). Current benches/README (ARM update 2022-08-27): Rust 1.62, clang 13, Skia v90; no extra flags on ARM.
corrections.hardware: AMD 3700X (Ryzen 7, Gentoo Linux) for x86-64 results; Apple M1 for ARM results
corrections.caveats: Rust library (language-filter mismatch). Slower than Skia on its own benchmarks; the claim is relative to cairo (and raqote) only. Results are old (x86 page July 2021, ARM page Aug 2022) and the current benches/README environment block (Rust 1.62, clang 13, Skia v90) was written for the 2022 ARM run, not the x86 page; cairo's build is a distro package with only -march=native stated (macOS cairo build for the ARM run not described). Cairo is faster on solid rect fills and nearest-neighbour patterns in tiny-skia's own data. The Vello CPU master thesis (LaurenzV/master-thesis main.pdf, M1 Pro, Blend2D harness with tiny_skia_c bindings, times per 1000 render calls) shows the same split: cairo faster on Fill-Solid-RectA (256x256: 18.6 ms vs 136 ms) and RectU, nearest-neighbour patterns and larger linear-gradient rects, while tiny-skia is about 1.1-2.3x faster than cairo on PolyNZi40 (small sizes), Fish and World fills and on World and Butterfly strokes; tiny-skia is slower than Skia and Vello CPU in most shown tests.

notes: Results pages on linebender.github.io are blocked but the same files are on the gh-pages branch via raw.githubusercontent.com; the per-test data supports 'faster than cairo in many cases' with stated compilers, flags and CPUs, hence the upgrade to A. Cairo build details are thin (system package), so the orchestrator may prefer B/C if strict about baseline flags.
